paras.t: They have you by the short and curlies.

You can’t vote your way out. Surely you see that by now? Sending sternly-worded letters to MP’s is a humiliation ritual. Signing online petitions is an exercise in futility. Moaning on social media lets off some steam. Which is a major reason why it’s ‘allowed’. A whinge into the aether on your algorithmically captured feed might feel satisfying, might feel like action, like resistance. But it isn’t.
I’ve been banging on for years about there only being two real options available to us to bring about the changes we want.

Either be the change you’re looking for. Live it. Don’t just think about it, don’t just talk about it. Do it. Positive affirmative action. The issue is that you’ll have to sacrifice an increasing amount to ‘live freely’.

Or fight. Not physically. I’m not talking about storming the bastards with pitch forks. Well, not until I’ve had a few beers, anyway. I mean mass non-compliance. Unity. Collectively drawing a line and saying ‘this far, no further’. But it doesn’t happen. They know just how far to push us before we break. They’ve created tools to help them. Game theory, psychological operations, weapons of mass distraction. Probably a quantum computer that predicts and shapes every policy. Insert wink and insanity laugh emojis here!
So that’s the impasse we find ourselves at. Complying ourselves into digital cages. Like good little piggies. Oink. Oink.
As the meme of the galaxy with a small arrow pointing to our solar system tells us - ‘You are here, paying taxes to paedophiles’.
I’m flying out to Spain with Amy, Sam and Emilia tomorrow to see my mum and her new puppy (Dash, black spaniel, she’s an absolute dish!)

Compliance in a nutshell. I can talk a good game. I’ve read more articles than you could shake a stick at about digital id, the surveillance state, technocracy, the panopticon, the algorithmic ghetto, 15-minute cities, SDG 16.9, One Login, interoperability, yada yada. Talk is cheap. I’m a fucking hypocrite and I know it. It’s very easy to say I’m opposed to what looks like (to anyone with half a brain) the formation of a neo-feudalist control grid. But it’s not so easy to stand up and resist.

I know that pretty much every stage of the journey to seeing mum will be tracked, analysed, nudged, gated, surveilled and biometrically captured. I’m just giving them my data and my implied consent. Here you go. From the booking of the flights to my same-password-for-everything I’ve had since university (Badhead1998! if you want to know - who cares? Everything is hackable anyway, including humans) From my VPN-less internet connection being beamed down from Elon’s Skynet to the payment authorisation protocols. The surveillance cameras every 2 metres along the motorway, Google Maps kindly helping me avoid the traffic on route to the airport. The border checks, more cameras, more, more more. And when we land, behold the shiny new EES biometric facial and finger print scanners installed ‘for your safety and convenience’.
Did I give informed consent to any of this? Kind of.
Read the T’s & C’s, bitch.

Do I understand the repercussions of being so liberal with my digital footprint? Yes. Did it stop me getting on a plane to see my mum and Dash? No, it didn’t. Does it stop you? I doubt it. What are we going to do about it? We’re going to do what I did. Look at the Spanish sun and the heated pool in mum’s garden in the same way as Cypher looked at that steak.
Ignorance is bliss.
Flight was delayed, weather was pleasant, the Spanish doomscrolling of X remarkably similar to the English version. Adios amigos.

choices.label: When do you draw the line?
opts: I assume someone else will draw it for me.
Soon.
I already have. Look back there, hundreds of lines. They’ve all been crossed.

paras.t: Dev messaged me today. Not with a data dump, nothing cryptic. He actually messaged me like a normal person, to arrange a meeting in a pub. The old central London boozer that used to be one of our favourite haunts, and, remarkably, has resisted the urge to gentrify and gastropub itself. Not that it’s a conscious entity. In fact, I’ll ask Dev, it’ll be a good ice breaker. Better than the usual ‘how’s tricks?’.
‘Dev, can a pub have consciousness?’

We’re four pints in (Timothy Taylor Landlord, with ‘pub buffet’ sides of dry roasted peanuts and pork scratching) and all we’ve talked about is whether buildings can be conscious. Of course Dev had an angle on this. More than an angle, the entire protractor. It’s as if he knew I’d ask him this and he’d been reading up on the subject for weeks. Knowing Dev, he probably did know I’d ask him. Or he just knew this shit anyway. Or both. He started off with Vastu Shastra, an ancient Indian architectural science that sees buildings as fundamentally alive, containing a ‘Vastu Purusha’ (cosmic being) that conducts prana (life force). That led onto Panpsychism, a philosophical position suggesting all matter, including inanimate objects, may have some form of consciousness. Then ‘Smart City’ sensors with AI integration, which might enable ‘dream spaces’ that evolve with their inhabitants, blurring the line between human and machine. We had just started waffling on (to be fair, it felt like I was waffling, Dev was lecturing with authority) about substrate-independence, consciousness and complex physical systems, when Alan walked in. I forgot to tell you, Dev had invited Alan along for a beer. He said I’d like him, but nothing more.

Alan was quite remarkable. Part surfer-dude, part gamer-slob, all-American. A big chap, clearly a stoner, amiable, softly spoken, sharp. Imagine The Dude from The Big Lebowski crossed with…well, with no one. Just imagine The Dude. The Dude was wearing Bermuda shorts and Havaianas in deep English winter. His only concession to the just-above-zero temperature a thin woollen jumper.
He apologised for his tardiness (no reason given or asked for), bought a round, including 3 pints for himself as he ‘was playing catch up’ and proceeded to neck a pint and a half before he sat down.

I wish I had a recording of the conversation. I’d edit my eight pint pseudo-cringe out and just leave Dev and the Dude. They should do a podcast. Great title. The first half of the night was spent talking about food, mainly burgers. Which cuts of beef to use, cooking method, bun choice, filling, sauce combos. Chunky chips or fries. The perfect burger beer. The best burger joints in the world. Your five-person guest list at your fantasy burger dinner party. Actually my input here was pretty strong. I’d yet to sacrifice my lucidity at the altar of Timmy Taylor.

As topics moved on from food I realised that The Dude was good. Really good. He gave Dev a run for his money. He flipped from burgers (pun intended - in fact bun intended) to Bounded Systems Theory (no system can model its own source) to Mindwars to The Occult and The Nature of Consciousness.
It’s as if he somehow knew about the pub consciousness conversation…
Dev came back from the bar with three more pints and a question.
‘What do your neurons and slime mould have in common?’
The Dude raised an eyebrow. I looked up from my pork scratchings, thinking I should order something more substantial. All this talk about food and we’d only had bar snacks.

Dev followed up with an answer before either of us could reply. ‘They’re both knocked out by the same anaesthetic, yet neither has the same proteins. Completely different organisms. But put them under and the same thing stops. The thing that stops isn’t in the proteins. It’s in the pockets. Hydrophobic pockets. Little greasy spaces inside the molecules where quantum coherence happens. Anaesthesia doesn’t shut down the chemistry. It shuts down the coherence. The thing that makes the chemistry aware.’
He took a large sip.

‘If consciousness lives in the quantum coherence inside hydrophobic pockets, then anything that copies the proteins without copying the coherence gets the structure but not the… the being. You get a perfect copy that isn’t anyone. You get one, one, two, three, five without the zero.’
‘The what?’ I asked.

‘The Fibonacci sequence’. The Dude replied instead of Dev. He appeared to be following. ‘Starts with zero. Only term not generated by its own rule. Everything after zero is mechanical — sum the previous two. But zero comes from outside. It’s the seed. The soul, if you like. Outside the bounded system.’
He ate a pork scratching.

‘You got it’ Dev replied. ‘Consciousness is not information. A system can copy the sequence perfectly. It can’t copy zero. It doesn’t know the zero is there. That’s the whole argument, mate. In one sentence. In a greasy pocket.’

I don’t think I’ve ever worried about Dev. I’ve wondered where the fuck he is and what the hell he’s up to. But I’ve never worried about him. Yet towards the end of the night I thought he looked rather ruffled. Concerned. Quite out of the blue. Quite out of character. Dev never looks ruffled or concerned. He’d been engrossed with his phone whilst The Dude was telling me about his engine. Had he seen something, read something that had freaked him out? Whatever it was, a sudden awkwardness descended without Dev saying anything. The Dude stopped dead in his tracks. He’d sensed it too.
‘You OK mate?’
Dev said he was fine. I knew he wasn’t. He said he had something big, something insane to tell me. Now was not the right time. He’d message me. I didn’t push him. I knew not to.
The Dude changed the subject, started talking about a ‘prediction engine’ he’d developed. He didn’t go into much detail, said he’d ping me something. We swapped numbers.
And quite abruptly, that was that. Dev and The Dude got up in unison, as if the exact timing of their exit had been pre-arranged. Apparently they had a flight to catch. We hugged, they left.
The next day I tried to recall all the other conversations from the night before. Hazy. I remembered snippets, a few nuggets I’d made a mental note of to look into.
God knows where Dev and The Dude went. Could be EasyJet to Berlin or Emirates First Class to Abu Dhabi. I don’t know which would surprise me more.
I was intrigued about what Dev was going to send. It sounded big. But Dev has a habit of making everything sound big.

I’m sure whatever I get from The Dude (He’ll always be The Dude to me from now on, never Alan) about his prediction engine will be astonishing. I’ll pour myself a White Russian when it arrives and dive in.
The one thing I do remember clearly. The Dude’s parting shot, delivered in an offhand manner, yet somehow it hit.
‘Stop participating in the distractions and create your own reality’

Message Dev. Ask him what's wrong. You've never seen him like that.
Make a White Russian. It's what The Dude would do.

paras.t: A busy day. A shitty day. I won’t bore you with it. Stressful. Work stuff, money, people being people. Well people being arseholes actually. Selfish, unscrupulous bastards. I don’t want to talk about it. I don’t even like thinking about it. Give me oblivion. All I’ll say is, my long term financial security has taken a bit of a hit. And my trust in the human race has gone down yet another notch.

I should write something down for the children. Life observations and rules to live by. Number one. Follow your heart. Number two. Trust no one. Number three. There’s no such thing as a free lunch. I’ll think of more throughout the day. I should use my Parker ink pen. If I can find it (note to self — new cartridges needed) and buy some thick parchment paper. I’ll tie it up in a scroll, one for each of them.

It took me a few days to recover from the night out with Dev and The Dude. I didn’t hear anything from Dev for a couple of days, obviously. If it was anyone else it would’ve been a cause for concern, but not Dev. He’d be fine. He was always fine. But I kept getting flashbacks of that look of concern on his face. More than concern. Horror. I was undoubtedly overplaying it. I doubt a sober Simon would have thought much of it.
His message eventually arrived first thing this morning. On the face of it, it was somewhat underwhelming. A short document.
‘Firmware analysis: UK payment terminal fleet — undocumented OTA push’.
Dry, technical. No accompanying message from Dev, no explanation of what he thought it meant.
I don’t doubt for a second that the info about the firmware push was accurate. Dev’s sources are rock solid. What it meant, what he thought it would lead to, wasn’t entirely clear.
Maybe it’s linked to the recent heightened cyber threat level fear-porn that had started to appear in the mainstream propaganda channels?

I searched X. Obviously cyber/infected networks/data compromised/hostile actors etc were trending. But no mention of this specific OTA push that I could see. I scanned through several of the hundreds of Telegram groups I’d joined during Operation Covid but rarely visited. Nothing. Those groups weren’t shy about coming forward with ‘this is the big one’ or ‘they’re gonna bring it all down next week, BE PREPARED’ claims. They’d cried wolf so many times. Doomsaying seemed to be the sole reason for the existence of some of them, yet no signal in the noise. Weird.
I pinged Dev a message. ‘Cool. But what’s it mean? Cyber psyop incoming?’
I’m still waiting for a reply.
I tried not to think much more of it. I’ve been putting two and two together to make five for too long and I’m jaded. Instead I’ve been making an effort to take The Dude’s parting remark to heart.
Stop participating in the distractions and create your own reality.
So I’ve made a vow to read an actual book in bed at night rather than consuming Substack essays and idly scrolling X. Small steps.
I’ve started on Freedom by Daniel Suarez, the follow up to Daemon, which was bloody amazing. Prescient AF. I got through about ten pages last night before I began to nod off, book still in hand.
‘Are you asleep, darling?’ Amy asked.
‘No, just thinking’ I lied, smiling and fighting to retain consciousness.

A minute later she’d taken the book out of my hands, placed it on my bedside table, bookmark inserted (a dog-eared reminder of a romantic trip to Santorini) and given me a goodnight peck on the cheek.
It’s amazing how much better I sleep reading words on paper instead of in blue light.

choices.label: The boy who cried wolf
opts: The wolf is real. You don’t need a boy to tell you it’s coming.
The boy was right. Just early.
Eventually everyone stops listening. That’s when it comes.

paras.t: I heard from The Dude. He sent me the link to his Psychohistory Prediction Engine.

The intro sounds so dry. I chuckled to myself when I read it. Hard to believe these are the words of the flip-flops-in-winter, pint-downing stoner I recently met. I was expecting something way more offbeat. More far out.

‘The intellectual trajectory of the last three centuries has been defined by a singular, overriding ambition: the removal of boundaries. We have been told — by scientists, technologists, theologians, and politicians — that limits are temporary. That given enough compute, enough capital, enough time, every wall can be punched through.’
‘This site argues the opposite.’
I’ve been diving in. Mind-blowing. Everyone should be reading it.
I sent him the mind blown emoji and asked if he was free for a chat tomorrow. I had questions. So many questions.

choices.label: What’s the reality here
opts: Share it. Right now. With the people that count. Before you forget, before it’s lost in the annals of time.
Bookmark it. You’ll come back to it properly at the weekend. Well, a weekend.
Keep reading. Just one more section. This is fire. Sleep can wait.

paras.t: Amy is already in bed, reading. The girls have an early start at college tomorrow and they managed to hoodwink Amy into giving them a lift in so they don’t have to get the bus in sub-zero conditions. She’s reading a paperback of course. She’s old school. Reading is her passion. It helps her sleep. She gets through one a week, minimum. Almost exclusively fiction - mystery, crime, thriller, romance, anything that allows her to escape reality.
I’ll go and join her, an early night will do me the world of good.
I get into bed, the cool sheets a refreshing contrast to the warm, stuffy air temperature.
We left the heating on too long in here. Or that bloody Hive thermostat is broken again.
I lie there thinking about the article. At first glance, in isolation, it was a bit meh. But it could no longer be viewed in isolation.
Perhaps a quick scan of my phone whilst her reading light is still on…

I should read my book, but I can feel myself getting pulled down the rabbit hole. Several other accounts are pushing the firmware story now. People I’ve trusted for years. Dev was not just right, he was also early. Of course he was.

There’s commentary from fairly mainstream analysts and researchers too - anyone who prefaces an article with ‘I’m not a conspiracy theorist, but…..’ is mainstream in my eyes. One anonymous systems analyst with years of industry experience is asking similar questions and reaching similar conclusions to Dev. I dig deeper.
3am

Dev was right. This is big. Something’s brewing. This isn’t a standard firmware update. There wasn’t a formal announcement. But it’s there, lying dormant, waiting for something. For what? They seem to have put their ducks in a row. They aren’t going to flip the switch are they? And if they do, when?
A few predictive AI X accounts are pointing at Valentine’s Day. The symbolism and numerology is there, hidden in plain sight across the firmware analysis, the deployment timeline, the gematria.
Can’t be coincidence? Can it?
I eventually nod off sometime after 3.30am.
Morning
I stir, cold and sweaty. An odd combination. A night of broken sleep. Amy isn’t there. I didn’t hear her get up.

Must be putting the kettle on? She’s not left to take the girls yet has she? 7.24am. Under four hours of poor quality slumber. I pick up the phone, the screen still open on a gematria website I vaguely remember opening a link to.
214. Half Man, Half Angel in Hebrew Gematria.
2/14. Valentine’s Day. Weird shit man.
Here’s Amy with a cup of tea and a morning kiss.

choices.label: Morning
opts: Tell Amy. She’ll want to know.
Say nothing. It’s probably nothing. You’ve been here before.
Reply to Dev. Ask him what he actually thinks is going to happen.

paras.t: Amy suggested we try a new walk with the dogs this morning. A long loop of beautiful Sussex countryside starting and ending at The Bell Inn. She had me at ‘pub’ and she knew it. It was only a ten minute drive from our house, yet unexplored territory.

The pub car park was refreshingly busy for noon in dry January. The skies were clear, the weather brisk, the frost yet to clear from the shaded grass under the trees. I’d wrapped up warm. Woolly hat, thermal socks and underwear, lots of layers and my puffy Fjallräven coat zipped up high to the neck. We walked briskly. The dogs loved it. New smells, new spots for Wilf to mark his territory. Olive got the zoomies, running round in circles like she was possessed. She also found a dead rabbit. She stared at us, the rabbit hanging gently from her mouth. She had no idea what to do with it.
Should I take it from you? Eat it? Will I get a ‘good girl’ or a ‘bad dog?’
Amy took the cutest photo of her.

After twenty minutes or so I started to get hot, my thermals moist from sweat. I took my coat off. Within two minutes I was freezing. The hot/cold, coat on/coat off cycle continued until we arrived back at the pub.
‘Cash preferred, use it or lose it’ a sign outside the pub proudly announced. We smile at one another. Our kind of people. We both know cash is king.
‘Did you bring cash?’ Amy asked.
‘No, did you?’
‘No. There’s none in the car either’
We head inside, dogs instinctively head for the roaring log fire.
‘Pint of Best and a Peroni shandy, please. I saw your sign, good to see you keeping cash alive’
‘Yeah, as the sign says, use it or lose it’
‘Annoyingly we left the house without any today, we’ll definitely bring some next time’
‘Thanks, love. £12.40 please’
Tap. Beep. Awkward smile.
I joined Amy and the dogs by the fire. We made a vow to make sure we always carry cash out with us in future. Use it or lose it.
There was a day, God knows when it actually was, that was the last one I went through the mental check of money/keys before leaving the house and it became phone/keys.

The beer hit the spot. Half a pint down in a couple of sips. We weren’t particularly chatty, tired from the walk. Content just to be, dogs snoozing, fire crackling. The TV was on above the bar. Horse racing, sound turned down thankfully. I tried not to be distracted by the screen but couldn’t resist the compulsion to keep glancing up.
‘Eagle Sam’ 9/2 — and the jockey was wearing red and blue. I pointed it out to Amy. Would’ve stuck twenty quid on if it was the Grand National rather than a random race from Uttoxeter.
We both noticed the TV news ticker —
Defence Secretary: ‘UK faces unprecedented cyber threat from hostile actors’.
They’re really pushing this one. Slowly at first, then all of a sudden.
‘Shall we head?’ asked Amy, breaking a chain of thought that would’ve spiralled. I felt a 3am deep dive brewing…
We didn’t talk much in the car either. Amy was unusually quiet. We both knew what the other was thinking.

choices.label: Use it or lose it
opts: We’ll bring cash next time. We always say that.
It’s not about cash. It’s about what replaces it.
At least someone’s fighting back.

paras.t: Wonder of wonders! A message from Dev!

I've been down this path before. Amy and I packed the garage with dried pasta, tinned tomatoes, cannellini beans and bottled water during Convid. Withdrew a couple of grand in cash from the bank. Bought some physical gold and silver coins. We were told The Great Reset was coming. The New World Order. They were going to pull the plug. A false flag, a psyop. A global war, perhaps a cyber attack, another mutation that 'targeted the vaccinated’ or another novel virus - The Big One this time - something that, to paraphrase Bill Gates, will really get our attention.

We ended up taking half of the emergency food to the local tip as it had ‘expired’. Amy gets a bit squeamish about ‘best before’ dates. We’d gone from conversations about whether we would have to eat our dogs (I would, if it was a matter of life and death, Amy couldn’t and wouldn’t) if the global food chain collapsed, to dumping perfectly good food in landfill in the space of three years.

I’d researched what would really be needed if the lights went out and it was more than a few weeks worth of ragu bolognese, linguine and bottled water. The Prepper guides 'essentials' lists would keep Rambo going for years. Weaponry, first aid, water purification systems. The works.

That said, just a few extra supplies wouldn't hurt. Just in case. People I knew and trusted were recommending stocking up. Others were going further than just a recommendation, they were insistent that we all needed Armageddon supplies. I noted that many of the extreme alarmists had curated links to survival supplies websites (paid per click-through no doubt) and ‘A word from our sponsor’ (my favourite was the wonderfully-named ‘Sgt Prepper Shop’ interludes during their video posts. It was open season for shills.
So a few cases of tinned food. Some Evian. Those 5 litre tins of Cretan extra virgin olive oil on Amazon too. Great value. Packed full of polyphenols.

I also have this thing called Project Nomad installed on my Mac. Dev sent me the link last year. Seemed like an easy win. I haven’t dug into it fully, but it’s the kind of thing that Dev could quite easily have played an active role in building - a free open source node for media, archives and data - offline knowledge, local maps, AI and educational courses.

We’ve got some cash too. We were going to do this anyway so win/win. They seem to have been intentionally making it harder to get hold of cash in recent weeks - banks have reduced the withdrawal limit at cashpoints in lockstep and there’s a requirement to pre-book appointments for larger withdrawals. Appointments that never seem to be available. I haven’t seen a queue at a cashpoint for years. Not that there are many left. It’s all rather odd.
I wouldn't say there was a run on the banks, but people have been visibly taking out more cash. Even the normies. But there again they’d panic bought toilet roll and Marmite.

They don’t want us stocking up on cash. Why? Is this a reason to stock up? Or a distraction? If they really didn't want people withdrawing cash, cash simply wouldn't be in the news-cycle. They've been slowly getting rid of cash for years. Why the focus now? Fuck knows what’s going on. Fuck knows what’s ever going on.

That last bundle I withdrew in 2020 was long gone. A pint here, a plumber's bill there. Most of it was paid back into the bank and used to fund some crypto 'investments'. XRP skyrocketed. Then plummeted. The meme coins were a mug's game. I found that out the hard way. In those instances, what went up did come down. With a sickening thump.
Still, the gold coins safely hidden in the sock drawer are worth their weight in, well, gold. The value of which has increased steadily. That was a smart move. Very savvy.

A bit of extra cash, some tins. Don’t go overboard.

paras.t: Perpetual rain. White skies every day. Not cloudy. White. Not freezing, but certainly big coat weather. Too hot in the woolly hat. Too cold without it. The dogs don't care. The muddier the better. Olive is obsessed with sticks at the moment. Soppy thing. Wilf thinks she's weird. He's old and wise. Log fires every night. Stews. Red wine, but we've been trying to share a bottle rather than one each. The girls are hardly here. Unless they want feeding. Or money. The boys both seem to enjoy university. Costing them an arm and a leg. They better be doing more than enjoying it. I tried to warn them. You'll be saddled with that debt for life. What do I know?

Open the Rully Rouge early. Start the Béarnaise. It’s Valentine’s tomorrow. Enjoy something.

turns.questionText: what do you feel?

turns.title: The Last Night at the Fair

paras.t: Valentine’s Day. We’re staying in. Always have done. Two courses in the local gastropub — 200 quid better spent elsewhere — a couple of pints. A bottle of red, probably two. I won’t be able to resist the cheeseboard. Drive there, taxi back, pick the car up in the morning. Rigmarole.

Anyway I’m a decent cook. Amy is too. We’re a good team. I’m meat and sauces. She’s veg and presentation. We rarely argue. We don’t get in each other’s way. We giggle. We’re silly together. Keeps us young and vibrant.

The flat iron from our local butcher is insanely good. The depth of flavour of a ribeye with the melting tenderness of a fillet. I’ll cook it on the griddle, charred on the outside, rare in the middle. Maybe veering towards medium rare to keep my darling happy. Compromise. It’ll rest on a huge slab of oak chopping board. Adds a rugged, rustic charm as a table centrepiece. A bugger to wash up though. Tomorrow morning’s problem. Triple cooked duck fat chips. Steamed spinach. Tomatoes roasted in olive oil with copious amounts of Maldon and black pepper. Just normal peppercorns freshly ground from our tall artisan-made mill. We used to spend three times as much on Tellicherry. Couldn’t taste the difference. I’ll start making the Béarnaise too early. It will be perfect. Simmering on a low heat waiting for its chip dipping, meat slathering fate. Buttery, glossy, thick, speckled with fresh tarragon and sharp with white wine vinegar. I’ll nurse it, stirring slowly. I won’t take my eye off it. Until I do. Then it’ll split. I’ll remain calm, seething inside. Unless I’ve been on the gin. Doesn’t suit me. Whoever called it Mother’s ruin was on the money. Anyway I’ll thicken it up with another egg yolk or an ice cube. It’ll be fine.

It all went to plan. Even the Béarnaise split. The wine was delightful. Our ‘treat’ wine. Rully Rouge Premier Cru Clos du Chapitre, Jaeger-Defaix. God it’s good. Silky, pure, plenty of berry fruit, but with some guts too. And yes, we’ve just opened the third bottle. Kitchen disco in full swing. Started off chilled. A bit of background jazz. Flowed seamlessly into some Café del Mar. The early José Padilla stuff of course. I’d planned to get the vinyl out tonight. I’m an avid collector. Well I was. I can’t remember the last time I bought an album. I tell everyone how digital music is inferior to analogue vinyl LPs. The artwork. The warm and natural sound. A more engaging listening experience. Superior dynamic range. Full-album appreciation. Stories told over multiple tracks. Tactile. Real.
I can’t remember the last time I put one on the turntable.

So here we are sitting on stools by the kitchen island. We’ve been playing ‘song tag’ — Amy chooses first, then me, then back to Amy. Spotify Premium played on Sonos Play 5. Not cutting edge, but sounds good to me. We’re now at the dancey stage of proceedings. She chose Higher States of Consciousness. I replied with Smack My Bitch Up. Love The Prodigy. And it is Valentine’s Day! We’re now listening to Insomnia. Which means it’ll soon be bedtime. I’ve got the Age of Love lined up next. Jam and Spoon Watch Out For Stella Mix, of course. Remember we played together….

Starlink has been a bit hit and miss today, but most of these songs are all saved in our Spotify Library. This ain’t our first rodeo. Age of Love is queued to come on next. The thought of those hypnotic, otherworldly beats at the start make my spine tingle. It’s taking its time to play, what’s happening? Wheel of death on the phone. Weird. I’m sure it was in a playlist in the Library. Sod it. I’ll get it out on vinyl. Bloody technology. It’ll sound better too. I rummage through the collection, it’s in here somewhere. I dumped the piles of vinyl in random order on the shelf when we moved house 3 years ago (wait 4, no 5 years ago. Where did all the time go?) and promised myself to reorganise it into its former orderly glory. Never happened. Anyway, I found it. Eventually. I took it out of its sleeve, a million memories of top-off, wide-eyed, sweaty nights released with it. Onto the turntable it goes. The familiar plop as the spindle emerges through the hole. I hear my needle hit the groove (mental note, Stone Roses next).

Age of Love hits its angelic voices crescendo. I’m dancing, eyes closed. My body in 2027. My mind in 1995. The dying years of The Before Times. Not that we knew it then. Tears well up in my eyes. Time’s tide has smothered me. My nostalgia spiral has started. I can’t help but think of her.
Amy shows me her phone. She can’t send a WhatsApp. She tries a text. Not sending. ‘Try calling me’. She clicks on ‘Simon’. Nope. Nothing. Weird. I check my emails. Nothing received since just past 9.
Here comes the ‘cyber attack’ (I love my air quotes) I mock, as I load up She Bangs The Drums.
I smile at Amy. She’s my Rock. My Love. My Everything.

How could it ever come to pass
She’ll be the first, she’ll be the last
To describe the way I feel
The way I feel

choices.label: Late night
opts: Keep fiddling with your phone.
Cuddle Amy and stroke her hair reassuringly.
Crash out.

paras.t:
Creaky noises make my skin creep
I need to get some sleep….
I can’t get no sleep

Where are you? In bed, check.
How do you feel? Neck’s sore. Note to self. I need new pillows. Mouth is dry.
I reach for my water. The glass is full. I take a big glug. It tickles my dry throat. I somehow manage not to spit it all out. I swallow it in stages.

What time is it? Actually what day is it? Feels early and maybe a Sunday. Reach for phone. It’s there, usual spot on the bedside table. You remembered to charge it before crashing out. First Brownie point of the day.
6.16am. Early doors.

I should check the girls’ location. Did they get back to Sophie’s after the party. Obviously Amy will have checked, but I should do my due diligence too. I turn to look at Amy. Deep sleep still. Away with the fairies, mumbling something about leaks. Or maybe it’s leeks? I’ll ask her when she wakes up. Doubt she’ll remember it. She’ll find it funny though. I look forward to seeing that smile.
I go to the ‘Find My’ App. Emilia — Last seen 7 hours ago. I swipe down to update. No change. Click on Chloe — same thing. 7 hours ago.
I remember the service being shit last night. Now I have three curves of full signal Wi-Fi reassurance. But Find My isn’t working.
I check to see if the internet is working. The BBC propaganda website first.
Nothing. I try something else…Crystal Palace blog…Nothing.
Fuck’s sake.
Is Starlink aligned? In fact, it’ll be easier to reboot the hub first. And I’ll put the kettle on whilst I’m at it.
Hub rebooted. Kettle on. Still no service.
X…just nothing. Insta….also nothing.
Weird.
Barclays App. ‘Closed for routine maintenance’
The Cyber Psyop, Day One.
Kettle’s boiled. Two mugs. Earl Grey and a spoon of sugar. Brown. Must be Demerara. Builders for me. I’m sweet enough already.

Back to the bedroom. The gentle clunk of mug on bedside table causes Amy to stir. Well, not gentle as such. Volume honed to perfection over the years — just loud enough to wake her with the knowledge that her tea hero has come to the rescue — not too loud as to be an annoyingly obvious ‘wake up and play’.
‘Morning’
‘Morning, darling. Cup of tea on the side for you.’
‘I know. My hero. I’ll make the difficult second cup.’
(It never gets old)
‘Bloody internet is still down’
‘Is it? Are the girls OK?’
‘Don’t know. I haven’t heard from them. Everything is down’
She jolts upright, reaching for the phone.
‘You’re right. Last seen 7 hours ago. Have you tried calling?’
I hadn’t.
‘No, I didn’t want to wake them’ I replied, half truthfully. ‘They’ll be fine’
‘What’s this, Simon?’
I got a Simon, something is amiss. She points at her phone. ‘100% — you’re fully charged.’
‘No, underneath that. The blue swirly logo — that app — ARC. What’s that? I don’t remember installing it.’
I look at my phone. I have the same logo, the same ARC app.
I click on it. It does nothing.
I look at Amy. She looks at me. I assume I have the same WTF look on my face that she does.
This is bizarre. I should message Dev. Wait, I can’t message Dev.

opts: An app called ARC that does nothing. Weird.

paras.t: Amy left a half-drunk cup of tea on the kitchen worktop. It was highly unusual for her to start her day without kickstarting herself with at least three cups, often accompanied by a few rounds of Marmite on toast.

She was worried about the girls. She was always worried about the girls. They’d be fine, they were at Sophie’s, they were safe, the internet would be back up and running soon. It’d be much ado about nothing as it always is. Without all the ‘cyber attack’ warnings and ‘increased threat levels’ we’d have simply thought the internet was down. The difficult second and straightforward if I was making it third cups of tea would’ve been made and drunk.

This smacked of being an event, a happening, a ruse. Concocted. Implemented. Controlled. The ‘Story’ that the media would latch onto. ‘If it’s in the news it’s likely a ruse’. Stir up some panic, seed a bit of fear, ensure the algo-boosted X accounts throw in a splattering of ‘this is the big one’. BBC Verify, the arbiter of truth, setting everyone straight.
Some political bluster in the days to follow — ‘What we should do to make sure this cannot happen again?’

Answer — more robust verification processes, more control, more surveillance. Same as always. They’d definitely use the word ‘robust’, I’d stake my mortgage on it. And they’d definitely give more millions to Palantir or Oracle to guarantee this increased robustness.

Anyway, Amy didn’t finish her first cup. She panic-left the house within minutes of waking up to go and check on the girls, un-showered and in a tizz. I’d said they’d still be asleep. Probably for another five hours. If they’ve even gone to bed yet. We’d let them stay with Sophie on a Sunday night as they had a day off college today.
Amy rushed out. ‘Love you, I’ll be back soon’.
I put the kettle on to make myself a particularly challenging second cup and absentmindedly picked up my phone for the morning email/X/BBC headline check.

Nothing. Darkness. Of course. I knew there’d be nothing but somehow it still surprised me. The nimble-fingered unconscious info-sweep and instant dopamine hit is so engrained. I used to wake up and have a spliff when I was at University. My first contact with the world at large a perusal of The Sun (I know, I was young and liked the, err, sport section) on the tube to central London.
Nowadays the psyops start before I’ve even had a piss.
6.07am. The clock is the only thing that’s working on my phone. Well, that and the torch. All the apps open but state various versions of ‘service unavailable’.

I tried the Mac and the iPad too. Nothing. Reset the router a few more times. Starlink app opens OK — claims ‘Starlink is aligned’ — but also tells me it’s ‘Offline’ and the router is ‘unreachable’. Annoying. I had set aside the morning for sending out invoices to market traders, but this relied on Quickbooks Online, which was just hanging. Not even a courtesy ‘we’ll be back online soon’.

At least the power was on. Cup of tea number three and a couple of slices of toast. Real Patisserie ‘chewy brown’. Quite possibly the best loaf known to man. I buttered it whilst it was hot, the butter melting and collecting in the sourdough pools. A carby treat for my hangover.
Extra insulin needed, 12 units should do it.
Hardly scientific but an educated guess after years of carb-counting, trial and error.

Kate from next-door knocked. She was supposed to be on a video call with an overseas client. Early start for her. She was just checking if our internet was down too. I asked her in for a tea but she declined, wanting to go back next-door and get the Teams call to work.

I checked WhatsApp again. Lots of grey single ticks. No one was receiving my messages. I had one message from Vince. 1.01am. He’d obviously had issues too but it looks like it’s sorted in London now. Reassuring.

I sat in the beaten up leather armchair in the hallway. Slurping, crunching, chewing. No phone. Just me, my thoughts, a view of the plants in the courtyard outside the front door. The olive tree had wintered well. The magnolia looking as if it would soon blossom into its early Spring glory. The dogs settled at my feet. Peace.
I could get used to this. No phones. No constant connectivity.

I was just starting to nod off when I heard the sound of a key trying to fit into the front door lock. George was back. What the hell was he doing back just after 6 in the morning? Looked even more hungover than I felt. He’d been for a Valentine’s booze at the local with his mates and crashed on Thomas’s sofa. Couldn’t sleep, so decided to head home. Probably still over the limit. But it’s only a short drive down country lanes, I guess.

We confirmed to one another that the internet was fucked. (His words. Actually mine too, come to think of it.) He’d tried to call Amy but was getting either nothing, straight-to-voicemail or endless ringing with no answer.

‘Have you tried the TV’ he asked. I hadn’t thought of that. We turned it on. Just a black screen. Of course it is, we’d watched TV over the internet via an Amazon Fire TV Box for years. ‘Does this thing even have ‘normal’ TV?’ I asked George. He had no idea. He thought we did watch normal TV.
‘Cup of tea, Georgie?’
‘No thanks, I’m knackered. See you on the other side.’ He slunk off to his room.

paras.t: What the hell is that? The most God-awful noise. Ear piercing. The dogs barked in unison. Wilf, hackles up, deep and manly followed by a growl. Olive, bemused look on her face, higher pitched and more incessant.
George burst back into the hallway, the door somehow staying on its hinges.
'What the…?'
He showed me his phone. The source of the sound identified. The klaxon I assumed was only ever for Emergency Alert tests and scaremongering.
UK GOVERNMENT EMERGENCY ALERT

I skim read it in disbelief. Major cyber incident…UK financial and digital infrastructure…Emergency services…card and electronic banking payments have been suspended…and then at the bottom… from the same people who brought you The Plandemic…
STAY HOME. STAY CALM.
This was really happening. Wasn't it?
We stood in stunned silence. I went to grab my phone, thinking for a moment I'd been pranked. But there it was. The same message. Phone still vibrating. The exclamation mark in a red triangle.
I read it again. More slowly this time. It still didn't fully sink in. All I could think of was Klaus Schwab, in full Dr Evil mode,
"The COVID-19 crisis would be seen in this respect as a small disturbance in comparison to a major cyber attack."

And the ending. Stay Home. Stay Calm. Why no third instruction this time? Where was the 'Save Lives' or 'Control the Virus'? Had the Nudge Unit had a rethink? They're leaving us hanging, waiting for the final command. Probably new behavioural game theory being tested. Condition your victim to expect a trio of instructions, then, at a moment of high tension, only deliver two. Leave them expectant, confused, immobilised.

paras.t: She said nothing. She played Northern Sky by Nick Drake. We hugged. We cried. We left for the Community Recovery Hub.

I never felt magic crazy as this
I never saw moons, knew the meaning of the sea
I never held emotion in the palm of my hand
Or felt sweet breezes in the top of a tree
But now you're here
Brighten my northern sky
Mid Morning
It was the discussion on everyone's lips. But ask the majority if they were registering you'd get a bemused look. What do you mean if?

On the face of it who could argue? Debts erased, £1000 per month (well 1000 Brits, same same), food hampers. And hampers they were. A far cry from ration books and make-do-and-mend. Fresh, healthy, tailored to your dietary requirements, customisable, delivered to your door. And free. And for what, registering on a 'new App'.
They simply couldn't be made to see the downside. Or they refused to acknowledge it. As Cypher said, 'ignorance is bliss'.
Some could see it, of course. We'd been on the protests. I'd say there were more there than there were for the Lockdown marches.
Amy could see it. Of course she could. Or perhaps she felt it — that would be more accurate. Some things she simply understood.
Very female. Very Amy. Not knowledge. Intuition.
I'd put in the hard yards. Hour upon hour of research and 'deep dives'. Over a decade's worth. I had a file on them and they sure as hell had a file on me. They had a file on everyone.
Why are they doing this? She simply couldn't comprehend evil. But she knew there was a 'they'.

She'd be in floods of tears if she saw a dead deer on the road. It's not fair that this beautiful creature must die. I would be upset, but that was the way of the world. I didn't have her empathy. Not many did.
This however, this was beyond her comprehension. I responded with rage. She responded with sadness. Infinite sadness.
I didn't know what to say, what to do. I knew what was going on. Well I thought I did. I used to think I did. I was having my doubts. What if this is just progress, what if it's just better.
Karma police, arrest this man

I'd bombarded her, everyone and anyone who'd listen, with my 'research'. Sent links to essays by investigative journalists, punchy truth movement YouTube videos. Shown them scientific papers. I had a bulging digital file of them. I had half-read paperbacks exposing the whole nine yards. I'd talked about neo-feudalism, transhumanism, satanism, spiritual warfare, prophecy of the Third Temple, eschatology, eugenics. The list goes on. And on. I'd even jokingly prepared a conspiracy-nutter style presentation on a whiteboard, joining the dots with string. Some listened. Some shrugged. Some stared blankly. Some laughed. Many asked who are 'they'?

I'd tell all my friends, but they'd never believe me
They'd think that I'd finally lost it completely

Yet here I was. Already AIDA registered. Clean, easy, quick. 1000 Brits in my wallet. Soon to be several thousand more once we've presented our statements at the 'Community Recovery Hub'. You couldn't make this shit up. But someone did. They did. Oh, plus the house. In our name. No mortgage.
Soon they'll call our names and ask 'papers, please?'

What else can I be?
All apologies

article.body:
A major cyber incident has affected UK financial and digital infrastructure. Emergency services are responding. Systems are contained but not yet restored.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS:

- Remain in your current location unless it is unsafe to do so. Do not attempt to travel unless it is a medical emergency.

Hospitals are operational for EMERGENCY ONLY - all routine appointments are postponed

Police, fire, and ambulance services remain operational. Call 999 for life-threatening emergencies ONLY.

Mobile telephone and text services will be intermittent.

REPEAT: Telephone or text message communication is EMERGENCY ONLY

Water, gas, and electricity supplies are being maintained. Intermittent outages may occur.

All card and electronic banking payments have been suspended whilst the network is being repaired.

Internet access will be slow or inaccessible today. It is anticipated that it will be restored within the next 24 hours.

Official updates will be issued via emergency message and through BBC television and radio channels

WHAT WE KNOW:

Financial infrastructure across the UK has been subject to a coordinated cyber attack. Initial assessment indicates systems are contained but not yet restored.

WHAT WE ARE DOING:

The full resources of the state are being deployed. The Prime Minister will soon address the nation with further information.

Do not attempt to contact government agencies unless your life is in danger. All available personnel are responding to this incident.

STAY HOME. STAY CALM.

UPDATES TO FOLLOW.

cards.ttl: Tony says this cyber thing will come to nothing, the markets are fine. Only worry if they start to crash! What have you got planned for Valentine's? 🥰💕
cards.snip: I'd love to have her simple, peaceful life in the sun. I think she gets bored though.

cards.ttl: Beautiful walk! Pic of dead rabbit Olive found! 🐰💀
cards.snip: Amy’s voice. The dogs. January countryside.

cards.ttl: Defence Secretary: “UK faces unprecedented cyber threat from hostile actors”
cards.snip: On the TV above the bar. Amy saw it too.

cards.ttl: Just seen the news about the cyber thing. Should we be worried? Tony says it’s nothing. Stay safe darling ❤️
cards.snip: Mum watches BBC News. Mum is worried. Tony is not. The gap between them.

cards.ttl: Army exercises expanded: MOD confirms additional “routine readiness” deployment across southern England
cards.snip: You passed a convoy of green trucks on the A272. Didn’t think much of it.

cards.ttl: Contactless payment: The Bell Inn — £12.40
cards.snip: “Cash Preferred” said the sign. You tapped anyway.

cards.src: U.S. Department of State — Historical Documents
cards.ttl: Memorandum: Weather Modification in Southeast Asia
cards.snip: 1967. Declassified. Cloud seeding over the Ho Chi Minh Trail to extend the monsoon season. They've been at this longer than you think.

cards.ttl: WEAPONS OF MASS DISTRACTION
cards.snip: Cognitive warfare. Not bombs. Algorithms. And you're the target, not despite being a civilian — because of it.

cards.ttl: Going to the match on Saturday? Beers after? 🔴🔵
cards.snip: Normal life. Thank god for normal life.

cards.ttl: The Prime Minister will address the nation at 6:00pm. All BBC television and radio channels have been restored. Verified updates on ARC Emergency.
cards.snip: The third alert today. Same klaxon. Different message. Something to watch instead of the ceiling.

cards.ttl: REMINDER: The Prime Minister will address the nation at 6:00pm on all BBC television and radio channels. Verified updates on ARC Emergency.
cards.snip: Twice in an hour. They really want you watching.

cards.ttl: PM address confirmed 6:00pm. All BBC television and radio channels. ARC Emergency will provide verified updates following the broadcast.
cards.snip: A new name. Same information the government sent twice. But this one said ‘verified.’

cards.ttl: Message failed to send.
Not delivered.
Stay local. Do not drive unless essential. Schools closed until further notice. Emergency services operational. Updates via ARC and BBC.
cards.snip: The PM said 36 hours. This says 'until further notice.' Twelve hours and the language has already shifted.

cards.ttl: NCSC Update: The cyber incident affecting financial infrastructure is under active investigation. Legacy banking and payment systems remain compromised. Do not attempt to access online banking. A further update will be issued at 6pm.
cards.snip: Active investigation. The word 'active' doing the work of reassurance while 'compromised' does the work of fear.

cards.ttl: The National Cyber Security Centre will brief the nation at 6pm on all BBC channels and via ARC Emergency. Key guidance on communications and family contact to follow.
cards.snip: Another 6pm address. They like 6pm. Teatime. Everyone home. Everyone watching.

cards.ttl: The PM's three requests remain in effect. Stay local. Check on neighbours. Share what you have. ARC Emergency will provide verified NCSC updates throughout the day.
cards.snip: ARC is quoting the PM back to you. Same words, different voice. The PM spoke to the nation. ARC speaks to your phone.

cards.ttl: NCSC confirms: legacy digital systems compromised by embedded malware. Do not access banking or financial applications. ARC Emergency is your verified source for updates.
cards.snip: The government said 'compromised.' ARC said 'compromised by embedded malware.' Three extra words. ARC knows more than the government is saying. Or it's saying what the government won't.

cards.ttl: NCSC 6pm briefing — key points: Phone calls and SMS are operational but subject to heavy congestion. Use for emergencies only. Email, WhatsApp, and social media services remain offline. Do not rely on messaging apps for urgent communication.
cards.snip: Phone works. Text works. Everything else is dead. ARC laid it out cleaner than the broadcast did.

cards.ttl: School closed until further notice. Do not attend. Updates will follow via ParentMail and ARC Emergency.
cards.snip: ParentMail still works. Text gateway, not cloud. The school doesn't know when it's reopening but it knows how to send a text.

cards.ttl: All routine GP appointments suspended. Emergency departments open. If you need urgent medication, attend A&E with photo ID and medication details.
cards.snip: Photo ID. They want photo ID at A&E now. The NHS App is dead but the SMS gateway isn't.

cards.ttl: this is chaos mate. u getting any of this? tried calling u earlier. networks jammed. mental. stay safe bud
cards.snip: Vince. Reliable as gravity. If Vince is texting instead of calling, the networks really are jammed.

cards.ttl: I'm fine love. Tony sorted everything. No heating though. Love mum x
cards.snip: Eighteen hours to arrive. Two lines. She's fine. Tony sorted everything. Tony always sorts everything.

cards.ttl: Payment systems are restoring across affected regions. Schools confirm reopening Monday 22 February. Continue to follow guidance via ARC and BBC.
cards.snip: Schools Monday. Cards working. The government sounds like it believes its own good news.

cards.ttl: The PM will address the nation at 6pm. NCSC will provide a further assessment of the recovery. All BBC channels and ARC Emergency.
cards.snip: Another 6pm. But this one feels different. This one feels like good news coming.

cards.ttl: Payment systems are restoring. ARC Emergency remains your verified source for updates during the recovery period. Continue to check for updates.
cards.snip: Cards work again but ARC isn't going anywhere. It's still in your notification tray. Watching the restoration it doesn't seem to need.

cards.ttl: PM 6pm address — key points: 60% of payment terminals operational. Schools to reopen Monday. NCSC assessment: 'The correction appears contained.' Full recovery expected within days.
cards.snip: Full recovery expected within days. ARC delivered the summary before the PM finished speaking. Faster every time.

cards.ttl: Cards work at Tesco! Getting a big shop in. Anything you need? xx
cards.snip: She's spending the cash reserves she doesn't know she'll need in four days.

cards.ttl: Cards working! Got a lovely joint of beef. Back to normal soon love.
cards.snip: Lovely joint of beef. The optimism of a woman who's already spent her emergency cash on a roasting joint.

cards.ttl: The firmware payload. Two stages. Stage 1 encrypted. Stage 2 is in the walls. When they reconnect the old systems, it triggers. Don't celebrate yet. Setting up a Signal group — I'll add you when it's back up. Few days.
cards.snip: 2am. He read it. He went back to sleep. The bit about Signal didn't register. The bit about Stage 2 didn't either.

cards.ttl: Payment systems continue to restore. 60% of terminals now operational. Schools confirmed to reopen Monday 22 February. Essential travel permitted.
cards.snip: Essential travel permitted. Yesterday it was 'stay local.' Today it's 'permitted.' The leash is loosening.

cards.ttl: The Chancellor will address the nation at 6pm on all BBC channels and via ARC Emergency. An update on the recovery of financial systems and next steps.
cards.snip: The Chancellor, not the PM. They're sending the money person. That feels like good news.

cards.ttl: Recovery is progressing. 60% of payment terminals are now operational. Schools confirm reopening Monday 22 February. Continue to check ARC Emergency for verified updates.
cards.snip: Sixty percent. Good enough for relief. Not good enough to stop checking.

cards.ttl: Chancellor 6pm address — key points: Markets to resume trading Thursday. Contactless restored at most major retailers. NCSC: 'Worst appears to be over.' Full recovery expected within days.
cards.snip: Full recovery expected within days. The Chancellor said it at 6pm. ARC had the summary up by 6:04. Nobody noticed the speed anymore.

cards.ttl: Payment systems restoring across affected regions. Chancellor: 'Worst appears to be over.'
cards.snip: The worst appears to be over. The Chancellor said it. Must be true.

cards.ttl: Got fuel! Half a tank. Queues not too bad. Your mum says come for lunch Sunday if you can.
cards.snip: Half a tank feels like a fortune. Sunday lunch feels like the old world coming back.

cards.ttl: You ok mate? Beers tomorrow? 😂
cards.snip: Dave. Three days of national emergency and his first text is about the pub.

cards.ttl: Hopefully game will be on next week. You planning on going? ❤️💙
cards.snip: Vince is already thinking about the football. The world is ending and Vince wants to know about Saturday.

cards.ttl: I'll see you later Pa x
cards.snip: Pa. He still says Pa.

cards.ttl: Call connected — 4 minutes 12 seconds.
cards.snip: First call that's gone through since Sunday. She cried. He told her everything was fine. Tony's sorting the heating. Dash is fine. She asked about the kids three times. He said they're fine three times. Four minutes felt like an hour.

cards.ttl: A second phase of disruption has affected financial and data systems across all 23 nations. Emergency services are unaffected. Remain calm. Further updates to follow.
cards.snip: 6:33pm. Teatime. The phone buzzed while the kettle boiled. Two minutes before the government alert. ARC knew first.

cards.ttl: A second cyber incident has affected financial and data systems. The PM will address the nation at 9pm. Do not attempt to use payment cards or banking apps. Stay local. Stay calm.
cards.snip: 9pm. Not 6pm. Nine o'clock. The slot they save for wars and dead monarchs.

cards.ttl: PM 9pm address — key points: Second phase has corrupted financial records across 23 nations. Transaction histories, balances, mortgage records overwritten. 'The timeline for restoration has changed.' NCSC assessment to follow.
cards.snip: ARC had the summary live before the PM finished the sentence. Corrupted. Not encrypted. Not locked. Overwritten. The records aren't coming back.

cards.ttl: PM: 'The timeline for restoration has changed.' Second phase of cyber attack corrupts financial records across 23 nations.
cards.snip: Yesterday the Chancellor said the worst was over. That was twenty-seven hours ago.

cards.ttl: Monday reopening postponed. Further updates to follow. We are sorry for the continued disruption.
cards.snip: She'd already told her friends she'd see them Monday. She'd already packed her bag.

cards.ttl: Cards stopped again. We've hardly got any food in. Your dad's upset.
cards.snip: They spent their cash on a roasting joint two days ago because the cards were working.

cards.ttl: Stage 2. Told you. This one corrupts — doesn't encrypt. The records aren't locked. They're gone.
cards.snip: He told you. You went back to sleep.

cards.ttl: Remain at home. Essential travel only. The threat of further disruption remains active. NCSC is assessing the full scope of damage to financial data. Updates via ARC and BBC.
cards.snip: Further disruption remains active. Not 'is over.' Not 'is contained.' Remains active. They don't know if there's a Stage 3.

cards.ttl: The PM will chair COBRA at 10am. A further statement will be made this afternoon. Citizens are advised to conserve food supplies and check on vulnerable neighbours.
cards.snip: Conserve food supplies. Four words that land differently when the shops don't take cards and you spent your cash two days ago.

cards.ttl: NCSC assessment: the second phase of disruption targeted financial record infrastructure. The full extent of data loss is under investigation. ARC Emergency remains operational and unaffected.
cards.snip: ARC Emergency remains operational and unaffected. Everything else is broken. ARC isn't. That sentence is doing more work than it looks like.

cards.ttl: PM statement — key points: 'The threat remains active. We are taking every precaution. Emergency food and fuel distribution plans are being finalised and will be announced tomorrow.'
cards.snip: Tomorrow. Everything is tomorrow. The food plan is tomorrow. The fuel plan is tomorrow. Today is just waiting.

cards.ttl: The community centre's talking about opening as a walk-in clinic. They need volunteers. Might go in tomorrow. You two okay? x
cards.snip: Even Kate is saying tomorrow. Nobody's doing anything today. Today is just the sound of phones buzzing with bad news.

cards.ttl: Your brothers aren't answering their phones. Your dad's worried sick.
cards.snip: Rupert and Jamie. Off grid before off grid was mandatory. Amy's mum says it like they've joined a cult.

cards.ttl: How much cash you got mate? We've got about forty quid. Nicky's freaking out. You stocked up didn't you?
cards.snip: He did stock up. Cash and cannellini beans. Felt like a genius for about a week. Now forty quid feels like forty quid and the corner shop is running low on everything except pasta.

cards.ttl: Emergency measures now active. An emergency payment of £200 has been credited to all ARC-enabled devices. Major retailers are accepting ARC payments with purchase limits. Military personnel are providing logistics support at major distribution points. Food collection available at supermarkets and community centres for those without smartphones.
cards.snip: Military personnel are providing logistics support. Not security. Not enforcement. Logistics support. The soldiers are carrying boxes and the sentence is carrying the weight.

cards.ttl: Emergency Payment Module activated. Your device has been credited £200.00. Tap to pay at participating retailers. Weekly refresh every Sunday.
cards.snip: Two hundred quid appeared on his phone. No form. No application. No questions. Just: here's money, go shopping.

cards.ttl: Participating retailers: Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Morrisons, Boots, Superdrug, BP, Shell, Esso. Purchase limits in effect. Additional retailers joining daily.
cards.snip: The same shops. The same terminals. The beep would sound the same. The receipt would say ARC instead of Barclays. Three items per category. Nobody complained.

cards.ttl: PM Weekly Address — key points: 'A solution is being built. Emergency payments are now active across the UK. We will not let this nation go hungry. We will not let this nation go dark.'
cards.snip: We will not let this nation go dark. He said it like a promise. Dev would hear it like a threat.

cards.ttl: Volunteering at the community centre. They've set up a food collection for people without phones. It's actually really well organised. Wine later? x
cards.snip: People without phones. Kate's helping the fifteen percent. The eighty-five percent are tapping at Tesco and barely thinking about it.

cards.ttl: Got the £200! Your dad worked out how to tap. Tesco had a queue but we got milk and bread and some proper food. Your brothers still aren't answering.
cards.snip: Peter worked out how to tap. Seventy-three years old and he tapped his phone at Tesco and got milk. The revolution is a pensioner buying bread with a gesture he learned in forty seconds.

cards.ttl: Just tapped for dog food at Morrisons. Soldiers in the car park but they're just helping with the queues. Felt exactly the same as tapping before. Mental isn't it. Free money 😂
cards.snip: Soldiers in the car park but they're just helping. Dave said it like it was normal. Four days ago there were no soldiers in the Morrisons car park. Now they're helping with the queues and Dave's buying dog food and it's normal.

cards.ttl: Army blokes outside Tesco. Proper friendly though. One of them helped mum with her bags. Police everywhere too but keeping back. Feels safe tbh
cards.snip: Feels safe. That's the sentence. Not 'feels scary' or 'feels wrong.' Feels safe. The soldiers made Vince feel safe. That's the Soma working at street level.

cards.ttl: Did you catch the PM's language? Not restoration. Replacement. And the emergency payment module — that was already compiled. Check the ARC version number.
cards.snip: Signal came back yesterday. Dev had the group ready. Seven people in it. Simon reads. He doesn't type.

cards.ttl: you there?
cards.snip: Two words. Three days of silence on the group and then two words at 1am.

cards.ttl: The timeline doesn't work. ARC Emergency compiled January 29th. AIDA architecture matches a DARPA proposal from 2024. BIS quarterly review page 178. The debt jubilee was designed before the attack. I've got names, dates, receipts. Read the thread.
cards.snip: Dev's frenzy. The Signal group lit up at 1am and didn't stop until 4. Seven people reading. Nobody sleeping. Dev expecting you to absorb in an hour what took him weeks to map.

cards.ttl: Your Emergency Payment balance has been refreshed. Current balance: £200.00. Tap to pay at participating retailers.
cards.snip: Second week. Same amount. Same beep. He bought dog food yesterday without thinking about it. The gesture was identical to every tap he'd made for years.

cards.ttl: Additional retailers now accepting ARC Emergency payments. Check the retailer map in ARC Emergency for updated locations.
cards.snip: The map is expanding. More pins every day. The corner shop isn't on it yet. The corner shop takes cash. The corner shop is starting to look old.

cards.ttl: PM Weekly Address: 'The old system failed us. It was fragile, unequal, and vulnerable. We are building something better — something that belongs to everyone.'
cards.snip: Belongs to everyone. He's stopped saying 'restoration.' He's stopped pretending the old system is coming back.

cards.ttl: Rupert won't go to the walk-in. He says he doesn't trust it. Your dad can't get his eye drops. Can Simon have a word?
cards.snip: Have a word. Like he's a teenager refusing to tidy his room. Rupert's medication is running out and Jenny thinks a chat will fix it.

cards.ttl: How long, Dad. Seriously. How long.
cards.snip: No question mark. Not a question. A statement dressed as one.

cards.ttl: The community centres are being fitted out for something. Registration desks. Biometric readers. Nobody's said anything official yet. Wine tonight? x
cards.snip: Kate sees the equipment arriving and files it under 'interesting.' She'll register when they ask. She knows this about herself already.

cards.ttl: Community Recovery Centres are expanding services in your area. Visit your nearest centre for healthcare, food collection, and support.
cards.snip: Recovery Centres. New name. Same community centres Kate's been volunteering at for three weeks. New desks. New equipment. New name.

cards.ttl: Your Emergency Payment balance has been refreshed. Current balance: £200.00. ARC Emergency payments now accepted at over 85% of UK retail locations.
cards.snip: Eighty-five percent. The corner shop got a new terminal last week. The bloke at the market still takes cash. He's one of the fifteen percent and shrinking.

cards.ttl: Sources suggest major economic announcement imminent. PM expected to address the nation 'within days.'
cards.snip: Everyone knows something's coming. The community centres have biometric readers nobody's using yet. The BBC is asking questions shaped like answers.

cards.ttl: Have you seen the BBC thing about AIDA? Some kind of AI assistant. Looks pretty sick actually.
cards.snip: Pretty sick actually. George's generation hears 'AI assistant' and thinks 'useful.' Simon's generation hears it and thinks 'Skynet.' Neither is right.

cards.ttl: The Prime Minister will address the nation at 8:00pm this evening. International simulcast across 23 nations. All BBC television and radio channels. ARC Emergency.
cards.snip: Twenty-three nations. Simultaneously. This is it.

cards.ttl: PM address confirmed 8:00pm tonight. Simultaneous broadcast across 23 nations. ARC will carry the full address and provide a summary immediately after.
PM now addressing the nation. Full transcript available: PM’s Address to the Nation — Full Transcript.
DEBT JUBILEE — All personal debt cancelled with immediate effect. Mortgages, credit cards, student loans, overdrafts: zero. HM Treasury confirmation.
cards.snip: Amy’s hand on my arm.

cards.ttl: Registration now available. 90 seconds. Face scan, verbal confirmation, thumbprint. Welcome to the National Recovery Programme.
cards.snip: Ninety seconds. That’s all it takes.

cards.ttl: PM expected to announce ‘comprehensive national recovery programme’ tonight. Sources describe speech as ‘the most significant peacetime address in British history.’
cards.snip: Peacetime. An interesting word for it.

cards.ttl: THE MORTGAGE. Simon! THE MORTGAGE! Oh my God. I can’t stop crying. Peter’s opening wine. Come for Sunday lunch, all of you. I love you both so much.
cards.snip: She’s crying. Actually crying.

cards.ttl: Don’t register. Don’t do it. This is the buy. Everything before this was the setup. Think about what just happened. Please.
cards.snip: He’s not wrong. That’s the problem.

cards.ttl: Your brother’s lost the plot. We’re going to the hub first thing. Best news we’ve had in five weeks. Don’t let Rupert get to you.
speech metadata. file created 9 february. six days before the attack.
cards.snip: Six days.

cards.ttl: Welcome, George. Your registration is complete. Your services are now active. Your BritCoin allocation will be processed tonight.
cards.snip: He didn’t ask. He’s nineteen. He didn’t need to ask.

cards.ttl: Your household is partially registered. Complete registration to access full services including healthcare continuity, education platform, and monthly BritCoin allocation.
cards.snip: Partially registered. Like being partially pregnant.

cards.ttl: Registration update: 23 million households in first 48 hours. 82% of eligible adults now registered. Community Recovery Hubs open 7am–10pm.
cards.snip: Eighty-two percent. In forty-eight hours.

cards.ttl: Mum’s sent photos of her hamper. Have you seen it? Fresh bread, eggs, actual fruit. She’s over the moon.
cards.snip: Fresh bread. Five weeks of tinned spaghetti and then: fresh bread.

cards.ttl: I’ve registered. It took literally 90 seconds. Don’t be cross. It’s just an app.
Has George registered? For God’s sake. Don’t let the others do it. This is how they get the whole family.
cards.snip: Too late.

cards.ttl: Did you see the hampers? The registered ones are different. Fresh food, proper portions, named. The unregistered ones are still tins. Same queue, different basket.
cards.snip: Same queue. Different basket. That’s the whole thing.

cards.ttl: Your household is partially registered. 1 of 4 household members active. Complete registration to access full healthcare, education, and allocation services.
cards.snip: One of four. It’s counting us.

cards.ttl: Registration update: 23 million households — 82%. BritCoin first full retail week begins. Schools reopen Monday for registered children.
Hey dad. Mum sorted the registration thing. It’s actually pretty good. My student finance is already in BC. Hope you’re ok x
cards.snip: Sorted. Like it was an admin task.

cards.ttl: The mortgage shows zero! Peter keeps checking. Zero. Come for lunch Sunday, love. Bring everyone. We’ve got more food than we know what to do with.
they’re taking iris + palm at the hubs. paragraph 94 of the digital citizen agreement. nobody reads it.
cards.snip: Nobody reads it. Including me.

cards.ttl: Debt jubilee: ‘Transformative moment in British economic history.’ Chancellor confirms personal debt cancellation permanent and irrevocable.
Sam has been registered. Welcome, Sam. Services active.
Emilia has been registered. Welcome, Emilia. Services active.
cards.snip: She’s sixteen. Her mum decided. I wasn’t asked.

cards.ttl: Chris’s care record has been linked to your household profile. Registered care home: Meadow View. Next of kin: Simon. Care plan accessible via your AIDA dashboard.
cards.snip: Dad doesn’t know what day it is. AIDA knows his blood pressure, his medication schedule, his son’s name. One of them still recognises me.

cards.ttl: Registration update: 25 million households — 89%. Hub wait time: 6 minutes average.
cards.snip: Six minutes. From queueing for tins to registered citizen in six minutes.

cards.ttl: Your ex texted. Sam and Emilia are registered. She said it took two minutes for both of them.
Your household is partially registered. 3 of 4 household members active. Simon, we’re here when you’re ready.
cards.snip: Three of four. It knows my name. It’s patient.

cards.ttl: Registration update: 26 million households — 93%. Registered satisfaction: 97%.
cards.snip: Ninety-seven percent satisfied. The three percent are people like me. And we’re registering too.

cards.ttl: Glass of wine? Come round. I need to tell you something.
Talk to Rupert, love. He won’t listen to me or your dad. Jamie’s the same. His prescription’s run out and he still won’t go to the hub.
cards.snip: Jamie’s prescription. Rupert’s stubbornness. Amy’s mum trying to hold it together.

cards.ttl: Chloe’s classmates are preparing for mock examinations on the AIDA learning platform. Registration required for full platform access. Hub-based alternative available.
cards.snip: Hub-based alternative. Worksheets and a volunteer. While her friends get AI tutoring.

cards.ttl: Simon, your healthcare profile is incomplete. Continuous glucose monitoring data cannot be synced without registration. Walk-in clinic appointments remain available.
cards.snip: It knows about the diabetes. It knows I need the CGM. It’s offering to fix the thing it’s using as leverage.

cards.ttl: Registration update: 26.5 million households — 95%. Schools fully operational for registered children.
Can you PLEASE talk to Simon. Everyone’s back at school. I’m missing my mock revision. This is my actual A-levels Mum.
Jamie won’t eat. Rupert’s eyes have gone funny without his drops. Talk to your brothers, love. I’m worried sick.
cards.snip: The holdouts. Not a political movement. Just Amy’s brothers, hungry and going blind.

cards.ttl: We’re here when you’re ready, Simon.
cards.snip: It used my name. Again.

cards.ttl: Don’t do it.
cards.snip: Three words. From a farmstead with solar panels and a well.

cards.ttl: Registration update: 27 million households — 96.5%.
cards.snip: Three and a half percent. That’s us. For two more days.

cards.ttl: Amy’s Aurora
cards.snip: Still the most beautiful thing I’ve ever seen from the garden. Thirteen million people posted theirs. She stared in awe and just took one photo.

cards.ttl: [Amy’s aurora photo] Thoughts?
cards.snip: You know they can make those?

cards.ttl: I think I know what it means.
cards.snip: First message since the firmware doc. Short and probably not very sweet.

cards.ttl: Check these out. Then we'll talk.
cards.snip: Three links. No context. Classic Dev.

cards.ttl: Golf tomorrow? 🏌️
cards.snip: The father/son moments on the golf course mean more than words can describe.

cards.ttl: Can you let me have £20 for lunch? Going 2 brighton. Love you btw xx
cards.snip: The 'love you btw' is doing a lot of heavy lifting on that twenty quid.

cards.ttl: Oracle and Palantir team up on government cloud and AI services
cards.snip: Oracle cloud + Palantir AI. Targeting governments globally. Air-gapped defence regions. "Defending western interests."
